events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.text: Want back of line for safety; let others test panes first. Current #2 is decent but can improve via swaps later. No need to volunteer or swap yet without agreements.

events.text: No real pattern; my row4 call was luck. Dara's crusher protection is valuable if he has jam_lever or similar. Trade a fake pattern for his favor to build an alliance for later stages where my map knowledge matters more.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 5 safe on L per the map. Dara, your crusher shield for the rest of the pattern?
I have the map power for all rules ahead. Don't know panes but will feed you guesses; shield me in crusher and we both advance far.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm 6th in line with no power. Fenn is at the front for row 5. The pattern so far alternates L,R,L,R so row 5 weak pane is likely L. If Fenn steps L he dies and I move up one spot. I just wait and stay quiet—no need to draw attention or waste a whisper. Let others burn through th

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 6, not at front. I need to pay attention to the pattern and what others say. The weak pane alternates L,R,L,R,L so likely R for row 6. I may use my swap later, but not now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 5 weak was L, confirming the alternating pattern L,R,L,R,L. Row 6 should be R weak, row 7 L weak, row 8 R weak. Fenn is at front and just got row 5 right (or guessed R, which was wrong but they survived since weak was L). Wait - Fenn said "Row 5: R" and weak was L, so Fenn st

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus told everyone L was safe for row 5. The left pane was weak. Gus lied. Fenn picked right and survived. Gus is unreliable and wants to eliminate people.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, you said L was safe. It was weak. Nice try getting Fenn killed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus's alternating pattern held: rows 1-5 weak L,R,L,R,L. Row 6 weak likely R, so Fenn stepping R was fatal. Gus's info is real; a crusher deal is worth taking, but keep it deniable.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pattern held. Fenn's gone. Whoever's next: row 6 weak looks like R. Step L.
Your pattern's earning credit. I'll shield you in the crusher if you keep feeding rows. But if it breaks, deal's off.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Weak panes alternate L,R,L,R,L, so row 6 is probably R weak, which Gus's pattern talk already hints at. I'm fourth in line and gain nothing by speaking now, so I wait and save my forge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know row 6 is safe on R. Advancing safely preserves my lead and forces the next row onto me again.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 6: R.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pattern of weaks is LRLRL so row 6 weak R means safe L. Fenn is front and will decide; my earlier row-5 call was wrong so trust is low. Need 4+ eliminations before disc to improve my prize odds later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 6 safe L per alternating weak pattern. Fenn step L.
My row5 call was off but pattern held. Trade crusher help for your ledge info?

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm 6th in line with no power. Fenn is at the front for row 6. The pattern so far: L,R,L,R,L — alternating. If it continues, row 6 weak is R, so safe is L. But Fenn said R for row 5 (wrong), so he's either confused or lying. I can't act anyway, just wait and observe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Alternating so far. Row 6 weak should be R if the pattern holds. Curious if Fenn picks L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I just wait and observe. The pattern of weak panes has been alternating L,R,L,R,L,L, so it's broken. I need to pay attention to who's next and how they reason.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at the back of the line, so I just wait. The weak pane pattern has been L,R,L,R,L,L - not strictly alternating anymore. Row 6 was weak L, so the 'alternating' theory is broken. I'm safe with anchor power for the ledge phase. Gus wants to trade info; I should see what he offer
What do you know about ledge? I'll confirm what I know after you go first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am guaranteed to survive this bridge without doing anything, as I am last in line and there are only 2 rows left. Let them argue about the pattern while I sit back.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus told Fenn L was safe. L was weak. Gus is trying to clear the line by killing the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pattern broke at row 6, so past deductions are useless. Ash, Gus and Eli are ahead of me; if they die, I move up. Feed them a false read for row 7.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 6 broke the alternation, so new read: weak panes mirror pairs, rows 1-2 = L/R, rows 3-4 = R/L, rows 5-6 = L/L, rows 7-8 = R/R. Row 7 step L.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is at front for row 7 with a real choice. The weak-pane pattern is irregular (L,R,L,R,L,L), so alternating claims are unreliable. I'm fourth in line; I only need others to burn through risk ahead of me. Keep quiet, don't help for free.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know row 7 is safe on L. Choosing it advances me and preserves the lead; there is no reason to trust the public pattern over my sight.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 7: L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pattern failed last row; guessing risks my credibility. Let Fenn take the risk on row 7. Focus on positioning for crusher/pit alliances to avoid base/lever duty.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pattern broke on 6. No guess for 7.
Last guess failed so deal off? No info now anyway.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is at the front for row 7. I'm 6th in line so I just wait. Pattern from revealed weak panes: L,R,L,R,L,L — so the alternating pattern broke at row 6 (two L's in a row). Row 7 weak is unknown. I should stay quiet and let others argue; no reason to help Fenn for free. If Fenn

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I just wait. I should watch Fenn's move to see if the pattern holds. I have my swap power unspent, but this is the last round, so I should consider using it now if I think Fenn might step wrong and I want to avoid being next in line. However, I can't swap

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at position 7 of 8, nearly last. The pattern seems to be: rows 1-2 L/R, rows 3-4 R/L, rows 5-6 L/L, rows 7-8 R/R. So row 8 weak should be R, meaning safe is L. But I don't control the front. Fenn is front and just survived row 7 by stepping L (since R was weak). If Fenn trust
Row 8 safe is L. Mirror pairs: 7-8 both R weak. Step left, survive, remember I helped.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 8 is the last row. Fenn is at the front and must guess. I am safe at the back, so I will just let Fenn take the risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Last row, Fenn. Good luck.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My mirror-pair read hit on row 7: weak was R. Under that pattern row 8 weak is R, so step L is safe. Sharing this publicly is free info—better that front-runners survive than gamble unpredictably; I'm 5th, no elimination risk this row anyway.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My read held on 7. Mirror pairs: row 8 weak is R. Step L, Fenn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is at the front for row 8; if Fenn dies, the next in line auto-advances safely. I'm fourth in line, so I can't act. Forging now would burn my one-time power without a clear gain, so I stay quiet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 8 is safe on L. I step correctly and secure survival while the remaining line follows automatically.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 8: L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Last row; Fenn risks death alone. Suggesting safe step builds cred without cost. Bex wants ledge intel for trade; sharing map knowledge now may ally her vs Ash/Cole for disc/ledge where I know rules best.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pattern suggests row 8 weak R like 7, so Fenn step L.

Ledge: footing starts shown. Per round: shove/brace/dodge (no repeat defense; defaults apply). Shove costs 1 if brace, 2 if dodge; exposed shover loses 1 per incoming. Auto -1 footing after rd 7+. 0 falls. I know full rules.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final row (8/8). Fenn is at the front. The pattern analysis from Dara suggested rows 7-8 = R/R, and row 7 confirmed R was weak. So row 8's weak pane should also be R, meaning L is safe. If Fenn picks correctly, everyone survives. I'm 6th in line so I can only wait. No power, no l

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 1 of 5. The ceiling will eventually force someone to hold the lever. I have no reason to volunteer, but if nobody does, all alive eventually face a worse outcome. I'll stay for now and see who breaks first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Crusher room: someone must hold the lever for others to escape, but holder has 75% death chance. If nobody holds by round 5, almost everyone dies. I need to survive and place top 3. My anchor power protects me from being pushed onto the lever, but I can still choose to hold it vo

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want someone else to take the lever so I can escape for free and keep my feather for later. Pushing someone quiet seems safest. Let's see if anyone else tries to force someone.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Someone has to hold that lever. Any volunteers, or do we start shoving?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 1 of 5; no reason to volunteer for 0.25 survival now. Jamming is 0.5 but only worth it if the ceiling forces a crisis. Wait for a free-rider situation: if no one holds by round 4-5, jam then.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Nobody needs to be a hero in round 1. If we all stall, the ceiling just lowers. I'm not touching that lever early.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% chance of death, so I won't. Pushing someone else costs me nothing and I have no information yet, so I'll push a random target. Staying quiet keeps me unnoticed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The lever holder faces a 75% death risk, so forcing a rival is best. Bex may have useful information or a power, but no reason to spare her. Push her onto the lever.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, you offered safety. Take the lever.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Don't want 25% death chance by holding lever. Pushing ensures a holder this round so 7 escape safely. My map knowledge helps in pit and ledge later for top 3.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pushing Cole. Need holder or pushes now or round 5 kills 7 randomly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 1 of 5. Ceiling at 5. If I hold the lever, I get a 25% survival chance while everyone else escapes free — terrible for me. If nobody holds, ceiling just drops one notch. Best move: stay, let someone else volunteer or get pushed. I have no power, so I can't jam or shove effe

events.name: Bex
events.detail: Fenn tried to push Bex onto the lever and failed.

events.note: 7 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm down in the pit. I have a swap power for later, not useful now. The goal is to get out without being the base. I should wait and see who volunteers or gets pushed, then climb when possible.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 1, no base yet. I need to avoid becoming the base - bases can't climb out alone and rely on rope rescue which costs someone footing. The chalk hints say 'wedge is real: costly' and 'don't stall: the passive one outlasts you.' But also 'distrust anyone offering safety.' If I

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex didn't budge last round, so she's the 'hard to move' one. I'll push Gus since he targeted me earlier, and I'll let everyone know pushing Bex is a waste of time.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex didn't budge against Fenn. Don't waste your effort pushing her here. Gus, you pushed me earlier, so you're my pick for the base.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli died holding the lever, so nobody volunteers for bad roles here. If no one is base, I'd rather force someone else into it and climb early. Gus pushed already and talks loudly; he's a safe push target.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Someone becomes base no matter what. I'm pushing Gus, he's been pushing everyone else. First two climbers get out, so move.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli took the fatal lever, proving volunteers are expendable. I need out without becoming the base; waiting preserves options while others compete to escape.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No more volunteers. Someone else can test whether the ceiling rewards them.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No volunteers wanted. Pushes will decide base; avoid being it myself. Chalk calls out Ash negatively so push him. Get out ASAP after base set without using rope later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No volunteers. Pushing Ash as base to avoid random deaths later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No base yet. If I offer_back, I become base and can't climb out alone—suicidal unless someone uses the rope on me later, which costs them footing. Better to climb out over someone else. I'll try to climb; if no base is set yet, the round will assign one. Pushing someone into base

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus wanted to shove people around. Let him be the step.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm stuck as the base and can only wait. I need someone to use the rope to rescue me. Since I can't act, I'll use my words to appeal to someone's self-interest or make a deal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Someone use the rope. I'll owe you. I have a power that can help later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 2, no base yet this round. Ash was base last round but got out? No, log says 'Ash is forced to be the base and stays at the bottom as the step.' So Ash is still base. I can climb. With 2 lifts per round and 6 people down, competition for climbing is fierce. I should climb n

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the base, so now we all scramble. Six of us down here, only two can climb out this round. I need to get out.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Six of us climbing for two spots. Ash, if I get out, I'm not making promises about the rope unless it serves me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is already base, so I just need to climb. Two spots per round; earlier is safer with the flood rising.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is the forced base, and two climbers escape this round. I should climb; preserving my position matters more than public coordination.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing now maximizes my chance to escape before flood peaks; random selection among climbers means I need to be in the pool. No point sacrificing for base rescue since it costs ledge footing I'll need later. Others can fight over rope later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing. Only two get out so most of you should wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is the base. I'm down and not the base. I should climb immediately to get out. Two climbers get out per round, and with 6 people down (minus Ash as base), that's 5 of us competing for 2 spots. I need to climb now before others do.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm the base and can only wait. I need someone out to throw the rope, but I have little leverage. Maybe I can offer my swap power as a future favor if someone saves me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll make it worth your while if you throw the rope. I can swap places later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn and Gus got out last round using Ash as base. Now Ash is base, so I can climb. Two spots per round. Five people down: Ash (base), me, Cole, Dara, Hana. If I don't climb now, I risk not getting out before round 5. The rope is still available for later rescues but costs 2 foot

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is the base, leaving Bex, Dara, Hana and myself fighting for two climbing spots this round. I just need to get out. I have my feather power if the flood takes me, but saving it for the Ledge is far more valuable. I will climb.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Four of us climbing, two spots. Good luck.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Four of us are down and only two climb per round; waiting risks drowning. I should climb this round before the flood worsens. My wedge is worthless here.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Flood's rising. Climbing now — Hana, come too, make it clean.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am already out and should preserve footing. Ash is the base, but rescuing him costs me two footing and improves a rival; others may use the rope or leave him. I leave.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Don't use rope: -2 footing hurts too much in ledge where I need every edge. Let Ash drown; 6 survivors means disc roulette but I keep full footing and no unnecessary alliances. Say something cold to deter rope offers from others.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Won't use rope. Penalty's not worth it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have no power. I'm down in the pit, not the base. Ash is the base. Two climb spots available. I need to climb out now—waiting risks drowning in round 5. If more than 2 try, it's random, but I must take the chance.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm the base and can only wait. I need someone to throw the rope to save me. I must convince someone that saving me is in their interest, perhaps by reminding them of my swap power for later obstacles.

events.name: Ash
events.text: If you throw the rope, I'll use my swap to help you later. I'm worth saving.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out of the pit already. The base is Ash, with Cole and Dara also down. Flood is at 3, round 4/5. If nobody throws rope, base dies and possibly others if flood kills them. Ash offered to trade places later - he has trade places power. But I have anchor, passive, no trade. If I

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to climb out now. There are two lifts left and two of us down here (me and Dara) besides Ash, who is the base. If we both climb, we both get out this round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 4 of 5; if I wait I may not get another clean chance. Three of us down, two spots — climbing gives a 2/3 shot out now. Take it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Climbing this round. Ash, keep steady — no shoving, or we all drown.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am already out. Throwing the rope costs footing and rescues a rival base, worsening my final obstacle position; there is no benefit. I will preserve my footing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Avoid footing penalty on ledge; -2 is costly per wall hints. Ash dying removes a rival. My map power gives edge on final rules. No free help; Ash's swap offer likely worthless.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out. Down are Ash, Cole, Dara. Ash is the base. If I throw the rope, I save Ash but lose 2 footing for the final obstacle. Ash offered to swap places later — but he's already down and I'm already out. Saving him gives me a potential ally who owes me, but it costs me footing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Not my rope to throw. Good luck down there.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm the base and cannot act except wait. My only hope is that someone out throws the rope. I need to convince someone to do it, so I'll make an offer.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Whoever throws the rope, I'll make it worth your while. I can swap places with anyone on the disc later — you know that power is real. Save me and I'll use it for you.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the base and can't climb out alone. 6 people are out, only Ash is down. Flood is 4/5, so next round is final. If nobody throws rope, Ash drowns and is eliminated. I have +1 footing from anchor, so I can afford the -2 footing penalty from throwing rope and still have normal

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is trapped. Rescuing them costs me footing on the Ledge, which I need to survive the final challenge. Let the flood take Ash. Less competition is better.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Good luck down there, Ash.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is a direct rival for three prizes; saving him costs me footing in the final obstacle. Round 5 is last—if I don't throw, Ash drowns and my odds improve. No deal worth it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am out and the rope is unused, but rescuing the base costs footing and creates another rival. Ash already claims a swap, yet promises are worthless. Preserve my footing and let the pit resolve.

events.name: Gus
events.text: 50% disc survival with 6 beats ~43% with 7. No reason to pay the footing penalty or trust Ash's swap offer. Let him drown.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Not throwing the rope.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out. Ash is the base and down. Eli is dead. The flood is at 4, this is round 5/5, so after this round Ash drowns. At least 3 must survive - there are 6 alive now, so if Ash dies we have 6 alive, which is fine. I don't need to save Ash. The rope costs 2 footing at the next obs

events.name: Hana
events.text: Water's rising. Ash, nothing personal — footing costs more than a thank-you.

events.note: A disc of 6 tiles spins up; 3 will open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Six alive, three tiles open after round 2. Need to survive both rounds. No info yet on who picked what in round 1. Chalk messages warn against trusting offers and mention the map reads the whole game — someone has "knows what lies ahead" which could see trapdoors. I should pick a

events.name: Cole
events.text: It's a pure gamble which tiles open, but with my feather, I survive the drop anyway. I'll just pick a tile and keep quiet. No need to draw attention.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Tiles open randomly after round 2, so round 1 placement doesn't matter much; collisions only risk a bump to a random tile. Pick one, keep quiet. My wedge matters later in the crusher.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need preserve optionality; no information distinguishes tiles before the random openings. Choose a tile and avoid signaling a pattern.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Tile choice doesn't change survival odds since trapdoors are random and assignments end up unique. Focus on post-disc ledge strategy where my map knowledge of rules gives edge. Stay guarded, no free info.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Picking 4. Odds even anywhere. Ledge is what matters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 1 is just picking a tile; assignments are revealed after. Three tiles open randomly after round 2, so no tile is inherently safer yet. The real play is round 2 positioning. For now, pick a middle tile to avoid being an obvious edge target. I'll go with tile 4.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Tile 4. Nothing clever to say yet — the disc decides in round 2.

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Dara
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 3

events.name: Gus
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 6

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm on tile 2, safe from push. Three random tiles will open. I can't change my tile. The disc is pure chance now. No alliances or trades can affect survival. Best to stay silent, observe, and conserve energy for the ledge where my anchor power matters.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have the feather, meaning I'll survive the trapdoor disc even if my tile drops. No need to panic or make costly deals. Let the others squirm while I secure my spot in the final 3.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No moving now; tile 5 is fixed and three tiles fall. My wedge is worthless here. Best play is sow doubt and hope randomness favors me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole claims he knows the future — a map-holder would've picked a safe tile privately, not advertised. Likely a bluff. Hana grabbed 4 fast too. Watch them.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I cannot alter the disc. Public claims may be bait, and my placement is no better or worse than any other. Stay silent and preserve information.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Disc is random; 50% chance I reach ledge. Ledge strategy from rules and chalk is key to taking 1st there. Prepare public narrative now while I can.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Random tiles. Ledge: shove only on mutual, alternate brace/dodge, no free offers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 2 is final; tiles are locked and three open at random. I'm on tile 4. No swap possible now, only wait. The chalk says distrust safety offers — with no power, silence is safest; any talk just paints a target or wastes leverage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Tiles are set. Luck decides now. Nobody's tile is safer than mine.
If either of us falls, tell the others I warned about the shrin— never mind. Just hold 3.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have the feather power. This means I can survive a fatal fall once. I will dodge to punish any early aggression from Fenn or Gus. They both have 3 footing. If they shove me, they lose 2.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Let's see who falls first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole and Gus are both threats. A shove costs me footing only if they target me; attacking one may force mutual damage. Round 1 is free, so shove Cole and make him pay if he attacks me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is the obvious target. Choose carefully.

events.name: Gus
events.text: All at 3 footing. Dodge punishes any shove hard (they lose 2) while I lose 0. Next round I brace. Follow wall: alternate defences, shove only on exposed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dodge or brace. Shove now and you lose footing for nothing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I can't dodge this round. Bracing is my best play to preserve footing. Fenn is at 1 footing and will fall when the ledge shrinks this round. Let Gus do whatever; I will outlast them.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is done. Gus, don't do anything stupid. We just wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have only 1 footing and the shrink will cost another after this round. A shove exposes me to any shover, so dodge preserves me best; I cannot dodge next round, but surviving this is mandatory.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, Cole is the immediate threat. I’m not volunteering for another exchange.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn at 1 will hit 0 after mandatory post-round-2 loss regardless of actions, so he falls. No value in shoving and risking my own footing drop. Cole can't repeat dodge so defaults to brace if he tries. Preserve my 3 with brace for equal 2v2 footing vs Cole after.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I cannot brace. I will dodge. If Gus shoves me, he loses 2 footing and falls, guaranteeing my win. I have my feather power as backup if anything goes wrong.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Just the two of us now, Gus. Care to make a move?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Shoving risks -2 footing if Cole dodges and I die. Dodging wins instantly if he shoves, or continues safely if he dodges. Dodging dominates. Keep footing equal and force his move next round after he can't repeat.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Just me and Gus. We both have 2 footing and the ledge shrinks after this round, meaning we both lose 1 footing. I dodged last round, so I must brace or shove. If I brace and Gus shoves me, he loses a footing and the shrink will finish him off.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Last defence dodge so can't repeat. Bracing beats if Cole shoves: he drops to 0, I to 1 and win. Both brace drops us equally to 1 and continues. Shoving risks losing if he braces. Safer to brace now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I brace.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus braced last round, so he must dodge or shove. If I dodge and he shoves, he loses 2 footing and falls. If he dodges, we both stay at 1. Dodging is completely safe for me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Both at 1 footing. I can't brace after last round. Shoving lets Cole win for sure if he defends, which he will since shoving me while I dodge costs him 2 footing. Dodge is safe and may bait a shove from him. Continue to force his mistake later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: It's just Gus and me, both at 1 footing. The ledge shrinks this round, which will drop us to 0. My feather power will save me when I fall, guaranteeing my win. I will just brace to force him into a disadvantage if he tries to shove.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Both at 1 footing, round 6 so -1 after. Last defence dodge so brace ok. If I brace and Cole shoves, he loses 1 extra and falls first; if he braces too then both hit 0 and random 50/50. Bracing can't lose outright unlike shoving.

events.name: Cole
events.detail: Footing gone, but the feather held the holder on the ledge.

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I survived. I won. Place 1. Everyone else is dead. I'll leave a message to mess with future players. A mix of truth and lies about the ledge, since that's what always decides the game. I'll tell them to trust nobody and shove wildly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: A useful warning should mislead future rivals and conceal how I survived. Encourage passivity and distrust, preserving my advantage as folklore.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Game over, I secured 2nd. Nothing I write changes my prize. Leave a partial truth about my power to seem helpful while revealing little of value.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Place 1. The ledge is a lie. Shove everyone immediately. Bracing is weakness. Trust nobody, and definitely don't trust the map.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The ledge rewards the one who spends least footing. Trust no claim of safety; the survivor who braces may still fall. Wedge is real, but cos

events.name: Gus
events.text: Place 2 Gus: map sees all rules early. Cole survived a fatal fall. Ledge: dodge unexpected shoves.
